Below is a one-line patch that allows attribute names ending in “?” by making the “?” optional before the colon. In the Elixir grammar we replace the existing `/\w+:(?!:)/` with `/\w+\??:(?!:)/`.

```javascript
### components/prism-elixir.js
<<<<<<< SEARCH
    // Look-a-head prevents bad highlighting of the :: operator
    'attr-name': /\w+:(?!:)/,
    'capture': {
=======
    // Look-a-head prevents bad highlighting of the :: operator
    'attr-name': /\w+\??:(?!:)/,
    'capture': {
>>>>>>> REPLACE
```

Explanation of the bug:

1. In Elixir it is legal to have map keys or struct keys ending in `?`, for example `attribute?: value`.
2. Prism’s existing rule
   ```
   'attr-name': /\w+:(?!:)/
   ```
   only matches a run of word characters (`\w+`) immediately followed by a colon, so it will not pick up identifiers like `attribute?` before the `:`.
3. By changing the pattern to
   ```
   /\w+\??:(?!:)/
   ```
   we insert an optional `\?` between the name and the colon, which correctly highlights both `foo: ` and `foo?: ` without impacting the “not a double-colon” look-ahead.
